analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (01.10.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -25bps at 7651 (+11.8% YTD) after a +2.5% quarter. Nasdaq is higher in 9 of the last 11 sessions despite higher rates.
US 10-year yield is at 5.28% despite softer inflation. Market pricing implies only a 36% chance of an October Fed hike.
Brent is lower at $97, gold at $4179, Bitcoin at $84k. Nikkei rose 3% on better macro data. ISM and Nike earnings are due today, and nonfarm payrolls tomorrow.

Micron reported revenue of $54.2bn vs consensus $50.9bn, with gross margin of 87.0% in line. Revenue and EPS guidance are above consensus, with revenue guided to $61.50bn at the midpoint vs consensus $57.6bn. The stock rose only +0.4% post market.

Micron management sees tight DRAM and NAND supply/demand persisting through 2027 and 2028, and says it has no line of sight to when supply and demand balance. It signed 10 additional long-term agreements covering ~35% of expected revenue through FY30. GS raised its Micron price target from $1100 to $1250.
Micron management says agentic AI workloads are already starting and are a reason server units are growing in the high teens.

Fed: GS no longer expects an October hike. Core PCE rose 0.25% in August and the yoy rate is 3.01%, below the expected 3.4%. GS now expects 3.0% Q4/Q4 core PCE growth, vs the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%. After comments from NY Fed's Williams, GS pushes the second hike to December and sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes additional hikes are unnecessary.

GS DRAM sentiment indicator for September is again moderately positive. DDR5/DDR4 pricing continued to rise, and Taiwan server ODM monthly revenue grew a record +130% yoy. Expectations for conventional memory and HBM pricing have been reset and have started to recover.

GS sees a tactical opportunity in the GSXUBOND basket (48 stocks), a long-duration equity expression with RSI below 30 and forward dividend yield above 4%. On five prior occasions with those conditions, 1-month returns averaged +2.7% with an 80% hit rate and 3-month returns averaged +5.9%.
Money market fund assets reached a record $8.44 trillion.
OpenAI is reportedly in talks to raise at least $30bn in a pre-IPO round at a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion.

Software fundamentals stayed healthy in 2Q. Median ARR growth moderated to 21.3% from 22.3%, and 20 of 40 sample companies accelerated yoy ARR growth. 2026 revenue was revised up for all four tracked segments, led by Infra/Platform.

GS crypto team: Bitcoin posted one of its strongest 3Q performances on record at +43%, despite 10y UST yields +100bps YTD, Brent +60% YTD, unresolved Middle East tensions, an FOMC hike of +25bps and the failed CLARITY Act. ETF inflows have supported it and the technical setup appears constructive.

GS lowered its year-end gold target to $4650 from $4900. Rates should weigh on gold through ETF demand near term, and central bank diversification remains the main structural driver. GS maintains $5400 for end 2027.
DoorDash unveiled an autonomous aircraft for end-to-end drone delivery, with pilots in Northern California with brands like Chipotle. Its AI agent also takes orders inside Apple's Messages app.
Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and ORCL has accelerated from 25% in 2024 to 48% in Q2 2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Core PCE at 3.01% yoy came in below the 3.4% expected, and NY Fed's Williams said there is no need for urgency. GS now sees no October hike and the second hike pushed to December, with a strong chance the FOMC concludes more hikes are unnecessary.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10-year yield is at 5.28% despite softer inflation. GS still forecasts a second hike in December, and the median FOMC participant forecasts 3.4% core PCE on a Q4/Q4 basis vs GS at 3.0%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core PCE Q4/Q4 trajectory moving toward the median FOMC forecast of 3.4% would undercut the case that further hikes are unnecessary.
